The image shows the different Mapleson breathing

ventilation?
e: Mapleson A (Magill circuit) is the most efficient Mapleson system for **spontaneous ventilation** because the fresh gas flow enters close to the patient while the APL valve and reservoir bag are positioned near the machine end. With adequate fresh gas flow, this arrangement minimizes rebreathing during spontaneous breathing.

q:
The airway maneuver demonstrated
in the image is:
e: The head tilt:chin lift maneuver is performed by placing one hand on the forehead and tilting the head backward while using the fingers of the other hand to elevate the chin. This moves the tongue away from the posterior pharyngeal wall and helps establish a patent upper airway. It is the standard basic airway-opening maneuver in an unconscious patient when cervical spine injury is not suspected.

q: The airway device shown in the image is:
e: The device shown is a nasopharyngeal airway (NPA). It is a soft, flexible, curved airway adjunct designed to be inserted through the nostril into the nasopharynx. It helps maintain airway patency by preventing the tongue and surrounding soft tissues from obstructing the upper airway. Unlike an oropharyngeal airway, a nasopharyngeal airway can generally be used in a patient who still has an intact gag reflex.

q:
A 45-year-old patient is scheduled for a thoracic
surgical procedure requiring isolation of one lung
for one-lung ventilation. The airway device shown
in the image is inserted to allow selective
ventilation of either lung.
Which of the following airway devices is depicted?
o: Single-lumen endotracheal tube with bronchial blocker
e: The image shows a double-lumen endobronchial tube, which has two separate lumens: one terminates in the trachea and the other in a main bronchus. It allows independent ventilation of the two lungs and is commonly used to achieve one-lung ventilation during thoracic surgery.

q:
A patient is scheduled for a short surgical procedure
on the upper limb. The limb is exsanguinated using
an Esmarch bandage and isolated with a double-
cuff tourniquet. A local anesthetic is then injected
intravenously through a peripheral IV cannula, as
shown in the image.
Which of the following regional anesthesia
techniques is being performed?
e: The technique shown is intravenous regional anesthesia (IVRA), also known as a Bier block. The limb is first exsanguinated and a double-cuff tourniquet is inflated to isolate the limb from systemic circulation. A local anesthetic, typically preservative-free lidocaine, is then injected intravenously into the isolated limb.

q:
A patient with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
requires high-flow oxygen therapy. The device
shown below is selected to provide respiratory
support.
Which of the following is the most important
characteristic of this device?
o: Delivers heated and humidified oxygen at high flow rates
Delivers a fixed FiO₂ using the Venturi principle
Provides positive-pressure ventilation through an endotracheal tube
Delivers aerosolized medication using compressed gas
e: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) delivers heated and humidified oxygen at high flow rates, typically up to about 60 L/min in adults. The high flow can meet or exceed the patient's inspiratory demand, allowing more reliable FiO₂ delivery. It also produces a small amount of positive airway pressure and helps wash out nasopharyngeal dead space.

q:
A 68-year-old man with an acute exacerbation of COPD
presents with severe dyspnea. His ABG shows pH 7.25
and PaCO₂ 68 mmHg. He is conscious, cooperative, and
able to protect his airway. The respiratory support options
shown in the image are considered.
Which of the following is the most appropriate initial
ventilatory support for this patient?
o: Non-invasive ventilation with bilevel positive airway pressure
Immediate endotracheal intubation in all cases
Simple face mask oxygen at high flow
e:
This patient has an acute exacerbation of COPD with respiratory acidosis and hypercapnia, indicating acute hypercapnic respiratory failure. In a conscious patient who can protect the airway, non-invasive ventilation (NIV), particularly bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP), is the preferred initial ventilatory support.
NIV provides inspiratory positive airway pressure (IPAP) to augment ventilation and reduce PaCO₂, while expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) helps maintain airway patency and improve oxygenation. It also reduces the work of breathing and can decrease the need for endotracheal intubation.

q:
A resuscitation training setup is shown in the image.
The device is connected to adhesive electrodes
placed on the chest of the manikin.
Which of the following best describes the primary
function of the device shown?
o: Automated external defibrillation with rhythm analysis
Continuous invasive arterial blood pressure monitoring
e: The device shown is an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) used during cardiac arrest. It analyzes the patient's cardiac rhythm through adhesive electrodes and determines whether a shockable rhythm, such as ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia, is present. If indicated, it delivers a defibrillatory shock.

q:
A 58-year-old patient under anesthesia suddenly develops hypotension and a rapid pulse. The ECG tracing shown in the image is obtained.
Which of the following is the most likely rhythm shown in this ECG?
e: The ECG shows a regular, rapid, wide-complex tachycardia with broad QRS complexes and no clearly identifiable preceding P waves. This is characteristic of monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) In a patient with a wide-complex tachycardia, particularly in the perioperative setting, VT should be considered unless a supraventricular origin is clearly established.

q:
A mechanically ventilated patient under general
anesthesia has the following capnogram:
The CO₂ baseline, which normally returns to zero
during inspiration, is progressively elevated with
successive breaths. What is the most likely cause
of this capnographic pattern?
e:
The capnogram shows a progressively rising inspiratory CO₂ baseline, indicating rebreathing of CO₂. In a circle breathing system, exhaustion or saturation of the CO₂ absorbent allows exhaled CO₂ to remain in the circuit and be rebreathed during inspiration. This produces a characteristic elevation of the inspiratory CO₂ baseline.
A normal capnogram should return to the zero CO₂ baseline during inspiration.

q:
The device shown is being used to deliver a high
concentration of oxygen to a spontaneously
breathing patient. Which feature is characteristic
of this device?
e: The device is a non-rebreathing mask (NRBM). It has a reservoir bag and one-way valves that minimize rebreathing of exhaled gas. The inspiratory valve allows oxygen from the reservoir to reach the patient, while the expiratoru valves prevent exhaled gas from entering the reservoir and surrounding air from being inhaled through the mask. With an adequate oxygen flow, an NRBM can deliver a high FiO₂.
